out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: multiple squeeze bottles and seasoning shakers around the facility did not have labels on them at time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. PLEASE LABEL ALL SQUEEZE BOTTLES AND SEASONING SHAKERS BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Linens & Napkins, Proper Use
violations.observation: Linens (i.e. napkins, aprons, towels, table cloths) found used in direct contact with the following food item(s): wet towels were observed being used to cover cooked noodles in the Continental 2DR UPR cooler next to stove top.
violations.corrective_action: Linens may not be used in contact with food unless they are used to line a container for the service of foods and the linens are replaced each time the container is refilled for a new consumer. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT WET TOWLES CAN NEVER BE USED IN FOOD PREP OR FOOD STORAGE. PIC REMOVED THE WET TOWELS FROM THE NOODLES AND WILL STOP USING THEM MOVING FORWARD.

violations.title: Miscellaneous Source Contamination
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were found subject to contamination after receipt and during storage due to the condition as described: The ice machine at facility was dirty to sight and touch at time of the inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 through 3-306. PLEASE EMPTY ICE MACHINE AND CLEAN INSIDE OF ICE MACHINE BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION. THAI CAFE (Inspection Date: 06/30/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Observed multiple wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. PLEASE REMEMBER TO ALWAYS STORE WET WIPING CLOTHES IN SANITIZER BUCKETS BETWEEN EACH USE.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: rice scoop and rice paddle were being stored in a container of water temping at 75F at time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL UTENSILS BEING STORED IN WATER, THE WATER MUST TEMP AT 135F OR HIGHER. PIC EMPTIED WATER AND WILL LOOK INTO WAYS TO KEEP THE UTENIL WATER 135 OR HIGHER BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: DOK Cross Contamination
violations.observation: There is no certified food manager on duty and the person in charge was unable to describe the relationship between the prevention of foodborne disease and the oversight of the following cross contamination. A food employee with gloved hands was handling undercooked chicken, then went on to handle clean equipment and utensils without washing hands. The manager witnessed this and did not take any correction action.
violations.corrective_action: The person in charge shall understand that foods shall be properly stored to prevent cross contamination (no raw meats stored above cooked foods or produce). Cross contamination is a significant concern. All measures must be taken to prevent it including observing and training staff on how to avoid it. This was corrected by the EHS teaching the manager the importance for preventing cross contamination. THAI CAFE (Inspection Date: 08/07/2025) Page 3 of 5

out_items.name: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

violations.title: Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco
violations.observation: Open drinking containers used or stored in a manner that may contaminate food, food contact surfaces or utensils.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may have beverages in the kitchen areas as long as they are covered and consumed through a straw and stored in a manner that will prevent contamination to food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items.

out_items.name: Hands clean and properly washed

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. The food employee did not wash his hands after handling raw chicken.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. The EHS pointed this out to the manager and the employee properly washed his hands.

violations.title: Cleaning Procedure
violations.observation: Observed food employees using improper handwashing procedures. After handling raw chicken with gloved hands, a food employee rinsed his hands in the three compartment sink, then went on to another task. He claimed that rinsing his hands in the sink was washing them.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wash their hands and exposed portions of their arms by: 1) discarding used gloves; 2) rinsing under warm running water; 3) applying soap; 4) rubbing together for at least 10-15 seconds; 5) rinsing thoroughly under warm running water; and 6) drying with paper towels or air drying device. This was corrected by teaching the employee (and other employees present) how to properly wash hands and having him demonstrate it.

violations.title: Where to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee was observed cleaning their hands in the warewashing sink. The food employee “washed” his hands (he rinsed them under running water) in the three compartment sink.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands in ONLY a designated handsink. This was corrected by educating the manager and the employee on the importance of washing hands only in a hand sink.

out_items.name: No bare hand contact with ready-to-eat food, or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed

violations.title: Minimize Bare Hand/Arm Contact with Non-RTE Foods
violations.observation: Excessive bare hand contact with exposed food that is not in a ready-to-eat form. The food employee was observed taking partially cooked chicken from a large sink filled with water to cool the chicken with gloved hands, however he was reaching so deeply into the water that his arms and elbows were under it.
violations.corrective_action: The employee would need to completely wash his hands, arms, and elbows after completing this task. In the future, this task should be accomplished by using a utensils, and hands, in order to reduce the risk of contamination.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided or is not clearly visible at all handwashing sinks used by food employees in the employee only restroom.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. THAI CAFE (Inspection Date: 08/07/2025) Page 4 of 5

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw chicken, meats and eggs were stored over vegetables and other ready to eat foods in the walk-in and several refrigeration units.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. The EHS informed the manager how to properly separate raw foods from RTE foods.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: Raw chicken was stored over raw beef and fish in the walk-in and several other refrigeration units.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). The EHS advised the manager how to properly segregate raw foods by type and cook temperature.

violations.title: Segregate Damaged, Spoiled, Recalled Foods
violations.observation: Damaged, spoiled or recalled food stored in a location that does not segregate the product. Badly dented canned foods were stored with other foods in the dry storage area.
violations.corrective_action: Dented, damaged, spoiled, or recalled food shall be held in the food establishment as stated under 6-404.11. Do NOT store dented, damaged, spoiled, or recalled food with food that is going to be used for the consumer.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Before Use After Cleaning
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment were not observed sanitized: observed a food employee washing and rinsing several sheet pans and other food equipment at the three compartment sink, but did not observe him set up and use a sanitizer after washing.
violations.corrective_action: All utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use and after cleaning.

out_items.name: Proper cooking time and temperatures

violations.title: (2017) Non-Continuous Cooking Process
violations.observation: The following raw animal foods were not properly cooked using a non-continuous cooking process: thinly sliced raw chicken was being partially cooked, then cooled for later use.
violations.corrective_action: Partial cooking of foods has several requirements in order to keep food safety. One requirement is that the process has written procedures that have been approved by the Health Department. This establishment does not have such written procedures or approval.

out_items.name: Proper cooling time and temperature

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. Four large containers of rice in the walk-in that was cooked yesterday and placed there to cool were 53F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. The temperature abused rice was discarded. THAI CAFE (Inspection Date: 08/07/2025) Page 2 of 5

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: sliced lettuce on the prep top unit was 68F. Foods in the top of this unit were being stacked too high to allow for proper temperatures to be maintained.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. The lettuce was discarded. Do not overstock foods in the prep top unit. Foods won’t stay cold if the containers are stacked or overstocked.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: several sauces and other food products made on site and kept more than 24 hours were not date marked.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. The EHS informed the manager of the date marking requirement for ready to eat foods held more than 24 hours.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name. Several spray bottles of cleaning solution in several locations and a container of soap under the three compartment sink were not labeled.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. The EHS discussed this requirement with the manager.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: partially cooked chicken was being cooled in a sink full of water. Food may not be cooled under standing water.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. The manager stated she typically cools the chicken under ice, but that her ice machine was down. If cooling under ice, the ice must be drained. If cooling under water, the water must be running.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: several large and small containers of food in working containers were not lableled.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Miscellaneous Source Contamination
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were found subject to contamination after receipt and during storage due to the condition as described: noodles in an uncovered 5- gallon bucket were stored under and in front of the kitchen hand sink.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 through 3-306. The manger moved the noodles.

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: bowls were being used to dispense food ingredients; scoops with handles were being used in some instances, but the scoop handles were being left in the food.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Clean Linens Free of Food Residues/Soil
violations.observation: Clean linens were visibly soiled with food debris. Most all the linens (wiping cloths) in use were badly stained, deteriorated, or both.
violations.corrective_action: Clean linens shall be free from food residues and other soiling matter. All stained linens should be replaced with new ones.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Safe Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not safe: food employees were using dishwashing racks to as colanders to drain food. Several manufacturer containers were being reused for food storage.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be safe.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not corrosion resistant, nonabsorbent, and/or smooth: soiled cardboard was being used to line shelving in several areas, including the walk-in.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. Cardboard is not an approved non-food contact surface. Remove the cardboard and clean the shelving.

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Smooth, Easily Cleanable
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not finished to have a smooth, cleanable surface: several cutting boards were badly scored, chipped, otherwise deteriorated and stained.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be finished to have a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Discard all the damages cutting boards and replace with new ones that are easily cleanable.

out_items.name: Toilet facilities properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned

violations.title: Toilet Room, Kept Closed
violations.observation: Observed that toilet room doors are being kept open. The employee only toilet room door was not self closing
violations.corrective_action: Keep toilet room doors closed to prevent insect and rodent entrance and the associated spread of potential disease. Install a door closer for the employee only toilet.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Observed the caps for the hood fire suppression system were either missing or not installed over the nozzles as required.
violations.corrective_action: Place the caps over the nozzles as required.
